MOZ.note: Says only that specific AI legislation is absent; nothing on harms rules or an authority.

facts.fact: UNESCO's Readiness Assessment profile says Mozambique has no specific AI legislation, with the Ministry of Science, Technology and Higher Education leading development of national AI policies.

MOZ.note: Nothing on civil servant digital-skills training.

facts.fact: UNESCO's profile lists a draft Cybersecurity Law among Mozambique's existing regulatory instruments, as a partial foundation for AI governance.

MOZ.note: Vodacom and Raxio investments are stated as aims; no data centre for hire in service is stated.
No national public digital-skills programme or measured skills share stated.

facts.fact: UNESCO's profile names the Electronic Transactions Law (2017) as an existing regulatory instrument in Mozambique.
UNESCO's profile reports the ITU figure of 19.8% of Mozambique's population using the internet, last documented in 2023.

MOZ.note: No nationally owned data centre for hire in service is stated.
Vodacom and Raxio investments are mentioned without amounts or dates.
Only the national electricity access share (33.2%, 2022) is given, not the rural share.
No school internet share or compulsory curriculum stated.
No STEM graduate share or research network connecting public universities stated; MoRENet is said to serve 106 institutions without naming universities.
